name: SPIRIT
aliases: Testosterone Treatment in Prostate Cancer Survivors With Hypogonadism
question: In symptomatic hypogonadal men with stable low PSA after prostatectomy for low-grade prostate cancer, does short-course testosterone cypionate improve sexual activity versus placebo without biochemical recurrence?

design.population: Men aged 40 years or older with low libido, erectile dysfunction, or fatigue; a mean of 2 fasting morning total testosterone measurements below 275 ng/dL and/or free testosterone at most 70 pg/mL; organ-confined Gleason 3+3 or 3+4 prostate cancer; and stable PSA at most 0.1 ng/mL (later at most 0.04 ng/mL) for at least 2 years after radical prostatectomy.
design.description: Two-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Design and Participants, p 806; Table 1, p 808

verdictNote: Sexual activity improved; no biochemical recurrence occurred during treatment or 12-week follow-up.
takeaway: In 136 hypogonadal men after prostatectomy for low-grade prostate cancer, 12 weeks of weekly testosterone cypionate versus placebo increased sexual activity (adjusted difference 0.91 daily events, 95% CI 0.56–1.26; P < .001); no biochemical recurrence occurred through 12-week follow-up (0/66 versus 0/64 treated).
